description: Source priority ladder, failure taxonomy, and health display contract for Career Seek job discovery.

provider_priority_ladder.label: Official ATS company pages
use_when: A curated employer source has a known ATS provider.
Google or manual import discovers an official ATS URL.
The role family maps to a curated employer universe.
provider_priority_ladder.display_notes: Highest trust. Results should show employer-owned source and provider badge.

provider_priority_ladder.label: Official custom company pages
use_when: The employer has an official careers page but no mapped ATS provider.
A known ATS page fails and the employer career landing page still loads.
The user manually adds a company name with a trusted official domain.
provider_priority_ladder.display_notes: High trust but variable extraction confidence. Show employer domain and verification state.

provider_priority_ladder.label: Google for Jobs discovery
use_when: Official sources return too few matches.
A company URL or ATS slug is unknown.
The user searches a broad role family across India.
provider_priority_ladder.display_notes: Fallback-only discovery layer. Live testing can hit auth_gate behavior; canonicalize to employer or ATS URL before ranking as official.

provider_priority_ladder.label: JobSpy multi-board fallback
use_when: Official and discovery sources fail or underfill.
The query is broad enough for multi-board recall.
The user explicitly requests maximum coverage.
provider_priority_ladder.display_notes: Recall fallback. Results require stronger deduping and source attribution.

provider_priority_ladder.label: Portal-specific fallback scrapers
use_when: Role family or user preference calls for a specific India portal.
Official sources do not cover the user's geography, seniority, or sector.
Freshers, blue/grey collar, government, or niche portal coverage is needed.
provider_priority_ladder.display_notes: Lower trust than employer-owned pages. Show portal source and ask user to verify before applying.

provider_priority_ladder.label: Manual URL or company import
use_when: The user provides a specific URL or company list.
A high-value company is missing from the curated source map.
Automated discovery fails but the user can identify the official source.
provider_priority_ladder.display_notes: Recovery path. Preserve user-provided URL, domain trust checks, and manual validation status.

failure_taxonomy.description: Expected selectors or structured fields were missing.
The source rejected automated public access or returned a blocking page.
The source requires human verification.
The source returned 429 or equivalent throttling.
Navigation, API fetch, or rendering exceeded the configured timeout.
The source requires authentication before job data is visible.
The source was reachable but returned no matching public jobs.
A required local package, browser, script, or API key was not configured.
At least one sub-source failed, but the adapter returned usable jobs.
The source changed URL shape, data schema, redirects, or rendering behavior.
The local browser automation layer failed before extraction completed.
The response loaded but could not be normalized into job records.
DNS, TLS, connection reset, or transient connectivity failure.
A provider API returned an unexpected 4xx or 5xx response.
A background job was left running or processing after a restart and was recovered by the worker.
The source appears to use an ATS that Career Seek does not yet map.
A manual URL could not be parsed or uses an unsupported protocol.
The URL does not appear to be an employer, ATS, government, university, or known portal domain.
The source indicates crawling restrictions that should be respected.
Results were reachable but too generic, stale, duplicated, or off-intent.
The source or result needs user confirmation before it should affect ranking.
The adapter failed without a more specific classified reason.

health_statuses.description: Source is reachable and returned parseable jobs or a stable empty state.
Source is reachable but partial failures, missing fields, slow response, or fallback extraction occurred.
Source failed the latest run and no reliable results were returned.
Source requires credentials, local dependencies, or user input that are not configured.
Source is intentionally off for the current role family, user preference, or risk level.
Source has not yet been checked in the current environment.

source_health_display_fields.description: Stable source identifier from provider_priority_ladder or portal adapter.
Official-first source priority, with 1 as highest trust.
ATS, portal, discovery, or manual provider identifier.
One of healthy, degraded, failing, not_configured, disabled, or unknown.
UTC timestamp of latest health or scrape attempt.
UTC timestamp of latest successful parseable result or stable empty state.
Short sanitized message suitable for logs and admin UI.
Number of normalized jobs returned in the latest run.
official, likely_official, portal_copy, manual_unverified, or unknown.
Confidence that title, company, location, URL, and apply URL were extracted correctly.
Employer, ATS, portal, or government domain used for trust display.
True when login, manual URL confirmation, API key setup, or manual validation is needed.
Retry boundary for rate limits, temporary blocks, or scheduled health checks.
Concise operator note for why this source is prioritized, degraded, or disabled.
